directAnswer: Check for merge conflicts and ensure that all tests pass before merging the pull request.
summary: Troubleshooting a pull request involves checking for conflicts, reviewing code changes, and verifying test results.

sections.heading: Understanding Merge Conflicts
sections.body: Merge conflicts occur when changes in the pull request clash with changes in the base branch. Review the conflicting files and resolve them before proceeding.

sections.heading: Reviewing Code Changes
sections.body: Examine the code changes in the pull request for clarity and adherence to project standards. Use comments for any necessary feedback.

sections.heading: Verifying Test Results
sections.body: Ensure that all automated tests pass. If tests fail, investigate the reasons and address any issues in the code.

steps.title: Check for Merge Conflicts
steps.detail: Navigate to the pull request in your repository and look for any merge conflict notifications. Resolve conflicts in the affected files.

steps.title: Review Code Changes
steps.detail: Open the 'Files changed' tab in the pull request to review the code modifications. Use inline comments for feedback.

steps.title: Run Tests Locally
steps.detail: Pull the branch locally and run the test suite to ensure all tests pass. Address any failing tests before merging.

faqs.question: What should I do if I cannot resolve merge conflicts?
faqs.answer: Consider reaching out to the author of the pull request for assistance or consult your team for help.

faqs.question: How can I ensure my pull request meets project standards?
faqs.answer: Review the project's contribution guidelines and coding standards before submitting your pull request.

faqs.question: What if my tests are failing after merging?
faqs.answer: Check the merge commit for changes that might have affected your tests and adjust your code accordingly.

caveats: Steps may vary slightly based on the version of the version control system being used.
